notes: Pass 5 (CWE-89 SQL Injection) candidate labeling only; 2609 source rows + 608 sink rows = 3217 candidates, all covered via 33 semantic groups (dedup) - see labels/labels_raw_pass5.json for the full row-to-group audit mapping.

Evidence verification basis: the CodeQL database source snapshot (django-db/src.zip, Django 4.2.0-alpha0, creation sha eb3699ea). IMPORTANT: the on-disk working tree at the source directory is stock Django 2.2.4 (git 8687fbe) and does NOT match the extraction CSV line numbers; all file:line evidence in these labels refers to the database snapshot, which the CSV rows match exactly (spot-verified at createcachetable.py:120/127, utils.py:66-107, compiler.py:1395/1657, query.py:1284/1670/1995, expressions.py:1049, sql/query.py:85/152).

This run is an in-context LLM labeling session (model glm-5.3 operating the Claude Code agent harness); no external LLM API calls were made. 12 batches were processed; per-batch scope and row counts are recorded in labels_raw_pass5.json.
pass 1 block: present with zero entries solely to satisfy the labels_schema.json 'passes contains pass_id=1' constraint; no pass-1 labeling was performed in this run.

Key semantic findings: (1) no framework request path feeds raw SQL text - request-derived values (admin ChangeList filters/search/ordering, auth, generic views) flow into ORM filter()/order_by() channels that compile to parameterized SQL; (2) the raw-SQL APIs (QuerySet.raw/extra, RawSQL, RawQuery(Set)) are genuine sinks but have no non-test call sites in this snapshot; (3) dynamic SQL in backends is built from quote_name-quoted identifiers, settings/DB-derived names, or CLI input - operator/DB trust level; (4) quote_name does NOT escape embedded quotes ('%s' wrapping only) and is therefore recorded as a candidate sanitizer, not a trusted barrier; (5) the bound-parameter argument is the proven sanitizer channel.

Extraction match_kind is 'ast' for all rows (receiver-name-agnostic matching); name-collision false positives (CLI .execute(), Redis pipeline.execute, error-message %-formatting) were identified and labeled none/fp individually.

entries.rationale: The <obj>.execute(sql, ...) call sites across django/db (ORM compilers, schema editors, backend base/introspection/creation/operations, GIS backends, sqlite _functions, cache backend) are the framework's genuine raw-SQL execution channel: SQL text is argument 0. Verified dynamic instances interpolate only quote_name()-quoted identifiers, settings/DB-derived names, or keep values in the bound-params argument; many instances are static literal SQL (PRAGMA/SET probes). The signature is a true SQL-text sink for pass 5; whether any instance's SQL text carries request-influenced data is resolved by the Phase 2 taint query - in this snapshot no framework request path feeds raw SQL text.
evidence: covers 220 sink rows (receiver names cursor/curs/conn/self/schema_editor) across 46 files
ORM endpoint: cursor.execute(sql, params) django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:1395 and :1657 (parameterized by construction)
schema editor funnel: cursor.execute(sql, params) django/db/backends/base/schema.py:199
static literal instances: django/db/backends/base/features.py:363-370 ROLLBACK_TEST probes, sqlite3/base.py:170/173 PRAGMA constants

entries.rationale: CursorWrapper.execute(sql, params=None) is the central PEP-249 funnel every backend cursor goes through (django/db/backends/utils.py:66); sql is parameter 1 (after self) and is forwarded verbatim to the driver cursor via _execute. A tainted string reaching this parameter is executed as SQL. CursorDebugWrapper.execute (utils.py:101) subclasses and delegates - same signature, deduplicated into this entry.
evidence: def execute(self, sql, params=None): return self._execute_with_wrappers(sql, params, many=False, executor=self._execute) - django/db/backends/utils.py:66
covers sink rows for CursorWrapper.execute / CursorDebugWrapper.execute definitions (utils.py:66, 101)

entries.rationale: CursorWrapper.executemany(sql, param_list) (utils.py:71; CursorDebugWrapper.executemany at :105, deduplicated) forwards the SQL text parameter to the driver cursor.executemany - genuine bulk SQL-text sink; param_list is the bound channel.

CursorWrapper.callproc(procname, params, kparams) - procname (parameter 1) names a stored procedure and becomes part of the executed statement, so it is SQL structure; the params argument is the bound channel. No attacker-reachable call site exists in this snapshot (cx_Oracle-oriented API), kept as sink for recall.
evidence: def callproc(self, procname, params=None, kparams=None) - utils.py:48

entries.rationale: CursorWrapper._execute / _executemany are the wrapper glue that carries (sql, params) from CursorWrapper.execute to the driver cursor (utils.py:82-94); modeled as taint step so wrapper chains reach the labeled sink.

SQLiteCursorWrapper.execute(query, params=None) (sqlite3/base.py:353) converts %s placeholders to ? via convert_query and calls Database.Cursor.execute. convert_query is placeholder syntax conversion only - NOT a taint barrier for SQL text.
SQLiteCursorWrapper.executemany(query, param_list) (sqlite3/base.py:359) - same channel as execute; query parameter is SQL text.
MySQLdb CursorWrapper.execute(query, args=None) (mysql/base.py:72) forwards (query, args) directly to the MySQLdb driver cursor - query parameter is SQL text.
evidence: def execute(self, query, args=None): return self.cursor.execute(query, args) - mysql/base.py:72-75

entries.rationale: MySQLdb CursorWrapper.executemany(query, args) (mysql/base.py:83) - bulk SQL-text channel.

Oracle FormatStylePlaceholderCursor.execute(query, params=None) (oracle/base.py:552) rewrites :name placeholders via _fix_for_params and calls the cx_Oracle driver cursor. Placeholder normalization does not sanitize SQL text - query parameter remains the SQL-text sink.
evidence: def execute(self, query, params=None): query, params = self._fix_for_params(query, params, unify_by_values=True) - oracle/base.py:552-556

entries.rationale: Oracle FormatStylePlaceholderCursor.executemany (oracle/base.py:558) - bulk SQL-text channel.

SQLCompiler.execute_sql / SQLInsertCompiler.execute_sql (compiler.py:1365, 1647) propagate the ORM-compiled (sql, params) pair to cursor.execute - summary step so ORM flows connect to the execute sink. Compiled SQL is parameterized by construction.
evidence: sql, params = self.as_sql(); cursor.execute(sql, params) - compiler.py:1382, 1395
insert loop: for sql, params in self.as_sql(): cursor.execute(sql, params) - compiler.py:1656-1657

entries.rationale: QuerySet.raw(raw_query, params=(), ...) (query.py:1284) is the public raw-SQL API: raw_query (parameter 1 after self) is executed verbatim via RawQuerySet -> sql.RawQuery -> RawQuery._execute_query -> cursor.execute(self.sql, params); only params is bound. Downstream applications passing request data as raw_query are injectable; no such call site exists in non-test framework code in this snapshot.
evidence: def raw(self, raw_query, params=(), translations=None, using=None) - query.py:1284
execution chain: RawQuerySet.__init__ -> sql.RawQuery(sql=raw_query, ...) -> self.cursor.execute(self.sql, params) - sql/query.py:152

entries.rationale: QuerySet.extra(select, where, params, tables, order_by, select_params) (query.py:1670) injects caller-supplied SQL fragments directly into the ORM query: select (param 1), where (2), tables (4), order_by (5) become SQL text; params (3) and select_params (6) are the bound channel. Fragment parameters are genuine SQL-structure sinks (documented unsafe API for user input).
evidence: def extra(self, select=None, where=None, params=None, tables=None, order_by=None, select_params=None) - query.py:1670-1678
clone.query.add_extra(select, select_params, where, params, tables, order_by) - query.py:1684

entries.rationale: RawSQL(sql, params, output_field) (expressions.py:1049) embeds sql (parameter 1) verbatim into the compiled query - as_sql returns ('(%s)' % self.sql, self.params); params (2) is bound.
evidence: class RawSQL(Expression): def __init__(self, sql, params, output_field=None) - expressions.py:1048-1052

entries.rationale: RawQuery.__init__(sql, using, params) (sql/query.py:85) stores sql (parameter 1) for verbatim execution in _execute_query; params (parameter 3) is bound.
evidence: class RawQuery: def __init__(self, sql, using, params=()) - sql/query.py:82-85

entries.rationale: RawQuerySet.__init__(raw_query, ...) (query.py:1995) routes raw_query (parameter 1) into sql.RawQuery; params (parameter 4) is bound.
evidence: def __init__(self, raw_query, model=None, query=None, params=(), ...) - query.py:1995
self.query = query or sql.RawQuery(sql=raw_query, using=self.db, params=params) - query.py:2009

entries.rationale: RawQuery._execute_query (sql/query.py:135) is the glue carrying self.sql/self.params to connection.cursor().execute - summary step for the raw() execution chain.

BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.execute(sql, params=()) (base/schema.py:170) is the DDL funnel used by every migration; sql (parameter 1 after self) is str()-cast and passed to cursor.execute. Callers across all schema editors %-interpolate quote_name-quoted identifiers into sql; collect_sql mode interpolates quote_value()-treated params.
evidence: def execute(self, sql, params=()) ... sql = str(sql) ... cursor.execute(sql, params) - base/schema.py:170-199

entries.rationale: Schema-editor mutation methods (create_model, delete_model, add_field, remove_field, alter_field, add_index, remove_index, add_constraint, alter_db_table, _alter_field, _remake_table, __exit__/deferred_sql, plus postgresql/mysql/sqlite3/oracle/GIS overrides) route model-metadata-derived table/column identifiers into SchemaEditor.execute - summary edges keep migration-state to DDL flows connected. Identifiers are framework/model-derived (operator trust), quoted via quote_name inside the template constructors.
evidence: covers 45 sink-csv wrapper-definition rows + 195 source-csv call rows across base and backend schema editors
representative: self.execute(sql, params) callers at base/schema.py:445-1135; spatialite/schema.py:69-188; oracle/schema.py:56-237

entries.rationale: DatabaseIntrospection methods (get_table_list, get_table_description, get_relations, get_constraints, get_sequences, get_primary_key_columns, get_storage_engine, get_geometry_type, get_field_type, _get_column_collations) propagate cursor + table_name/index parameters into information_schema/PRAGMA/SHOW SQL. Injection-shaped %-interpolation but inputs are DB-derived introspection names (second-order taint) usually quote_name-quoted; some sites use bound parameters instead. Retained as summary for second-order flow; manual review flagged.

Test-database creation wrappers (_execute_create_test_db, _create_test_db, _destroy_test_db, _clone_test_db, _database_exists, _execute_statements) build CREATE/DROP DATABASE/USER DDL from settings-derived names via quote_name'd %-formatting. Operator-level trust (settings.DATABASES and test runner config); summary edges only.

Backend operations helpers (execute_sql_flush, last_insert_id, __foreign_key_constraints, _get_sequence_name, __references_graph, _quote_params_for_last_executed_query, _get_postgis_func/_get_spatialite_func) propagate backend-generated SQL or model/DB-derived identifiers into the execute funnel. Inputs are framework-generated (operator/DB trust).
evidence: execute_sql_flush executes a backend-generated sql_list - base/operations.py:441-449
cursor.execute('"%s".currval' % sq_name) with DB-derived sq_name - oracle/operations.py:341
'SELECT %s' % func with constant spatial function names - spatialite/operations.py:151, postgis/operations.py:328

entries.rationale: Connection-state wrappers whose parameters can reach SQL text: check_constraints(table_names) -> 'PRAGMA foreign_key_check(%s)' % quote_name(table_name) (sqlite3/base.py:235-238), _savepoint(sid) -> ops.savepoint_create_sql(sid), ensure_timezone, disable/enable_constraint_checking. sid is a framework-generated counter; table_names are DB/introspection-derived. Summary edges retained with manual-review flag (second-order).

Wrappers executing only static literal SQL (init_connection_state, is_usable, mysql_server_data, get_new_connection, prepare_database, _start_transaction_under_autocommit, feature probes supports_transactions/supports_json_field/supports_collation_on_charfield, get_hstore_oids/get_citext_oids): their parameters do not influence SQL text - not pass-5 sinks. The genuine execute calls inside them are covered by the execute call-site entry.

entries.rationale: String constructions producing error/log/stdout messages, not SQL: management/__init__.py:116 ('Unknown command: %r'), :165 (f-string TypeError message), :185 (options error), management/base.py:411 (stderr formatting), sql/query.py:149 (RuntimeError 'Unexpected params type: %s'). Name-collision false positives of the sql_percent_format/sql_fstring extraction families.

entries.rationale: SQL template constructions (% / f-string / concat) across backends: interpolations are quote_name()-quoted identifiers, settings/DB-derived names, or preserve %%s bound placeholders (cache db.py:144-196, mysql/schema.py, GIS DDL templates, check_constraints REFERRING joins). Construction nodes are not execution APIs - the built strings flow into the execute-family sinks already labeled, and %-formatting taint propagation is standard CodeQL modeling; no separate sink entry is warranted.
evidence: bound placeholder preserved: 'UPDATE %s SET %s = %%s WHERE %s = %%s' % (table, quote_name(...)) - cache/backends/db.py:170-171
GIS DDL templates: self.sql_add_spatial_index % {...} - gis schema editors

entries.rationale: .execute() calls that are CLI command dispatch, not database cursors: management/__init__.py:198 (command.execute(*args, **defaults)), :446 (utility.execute()), management/base.py:402 (self.execute(*args, **cmd_options)), runserver.py:74 / createsuperuser.py:88 / sqlmigrate.py:38 (super().execute(...) on BaseCommand). Method-name collision with cursor.execute.

CLI dispatch wrappers (call_command, execute_from_command_line, run_from_argv) propagate operator-supplied command names/options into management command handlers; commands such as createcachetable (CLI tablename -> quote_name'd DDL), loaddata, sqlmigrate and flush reach the SQL layer. Operator-level trust boundary (manage.py is run by the deployment operator with DB credentials) - classification 'candidate' pending manual review of any environment where commands are exposed to less-trusted callers.
evidence: covers 3 sink-csv wrapper definitions + 14 source-csv call rows (call_command call sites)

entries.rationale: pipeline.execute() in django/core/cache/backends/redis.py:148 flushes a Redis command pipeline (set_many wrapper at :138 likewise) - Redis protocol, no SQL. Method-name collision with cursor.execute.

register() in django/db/backends/sqlite3/_functions.py registers Python callables as SQLite SQL functions via connection.create_function/create_aggregate - function registration, not SQL text execution.

DatabaseCache methods (get_many, _base_set, _base_delete_many, has_key, _cull, clear) build cache SQL with quote_name'd table/column identifiers and pass keys/values through the bound-parameter argument ([key] / [b64encoded, exp, key]); cache keys are make_and_validate_key()'d. Summary edges from the cache API to the execute funnel; value channel is parameterized.
evidence: 'INSERT INTO %s (%s, %s, %s) VALUES (%%s, %%s, %%s)' % (table, quote_name(...)), [key, b64encoded, exp] - db.py:188-196

entries.rationale: Management-command SQL wrappers: createcachetable.create_table(database, tablename, dry_run) builds CREATE TABLE/INDEX DDL %-interpolating the CLI-supplied tablename (quote_name'd via qn) and executes it (createcachetable.py:64-127); loaddata.reset_sequences and sites.create_default_site execute backend-generated sequence-reset SQL. CLI/operator trust - the tablename is the only externally supplied identifier; kept 'candidate' for manual review.

Migration operations (RunSQL._run_sql, postgres CreateExtension/Collation/database_forwards, model/field operations) forward migration-defined SQL and identifiers into schema_editor.execute. Migration content is developer-authored (operator trust); extension/collation names are quote_name'd before interpolation.
evidence: 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS %s' % schema_editor.quote_name(self.name) - contrib/postgres/operations.py:27-30

entries.rationale: The params/bound argument of the execute family (argument 1 at call sites, parameter 2 in wrapper definitions; likewise executemany param_list and callproc params) is the prepared-statement channel: values are substituted by the DB driver and cannot alter SQL text. This is the primary proven SQL-injection barrier for pass 5 - model as isBarrier at the bound-parameter positions so taint flowing into params does not reach the SQL-text sink.
evidence: cache values bound: [key], [b64encoded, exp, key] - cache/backends/db.py:151/172/185/196

entries.rationale: connection.ops.quote_name wraps identifiers in backend-specific quotes before %-interpolation into SQL text. Verified implementations do NOT escape embedded quote characters (sqlite3/postgresql: '"%s"' % name; mysql: '`%s`' % name) - quoting is adequate only for framework-controlled identifier character sets (model field names, introspected table names), NOT a strict input sanitizer. Recorded as sanitizer 'candidate' with manual-review flag: safe for the identifier families used at the observed call sites, unsafe as a general barrier for arbitrary attacker text.
evidence: sqlite3: return '"%s"' % name (no embedded-quote escaping) - sqlite3/operations.py:189-192
used at: sqlite3/introspection.py:94, mysql/introspection.py:310, createcachetable.py:77-100 (qn), postgres/operations.py:29/196

entries.rationale: request.GET (parsed QUERY_STRING via QueryDict) is the primary attacker-controlled input boundary of the framework's HTTP surface; attribute reads in admin ChangeList/autocompletion, generic date views, i18n and middleware are genuine pass-5 source nodes. Downstream framework consumption compiles to parameterized ORM SQL (admin filters/ordering), so sources are real but the observed channels are safe.
request.POST (parsed request body via QueryDict/multipart) - attacker-controlled HTTP input boundary; read sites in admin options (form data, action selections), middleware and auth.

request.META (WSGI environ-derived headers/CGI vars) - attacker-influenced HTTP header boundary (including CSRF_COOKIE populated from cookie/header). Read sites in csrf/cache/common middleware, debug views, admin.
request.COOKIES - attacker-controlled cookie boundary (session/csrf/cache-key material); framework consumers feed cache keys (validated) and session lookups, not raw SQL.
request.FILES - multipart-uploaded file metadata/content boundary; consumed by multipart parser and file storage, no observed path into SQL text.

The raw WSGI environ dict is the lowest-trust input boundary of the framework: WSGIRequest.__init__ derives request.META/GET/POST from it; environ.get/keys reads in handlers (wsgi.py:144 environ.get('wsgi.file_wrapper')) and dev servers are genuine source nodes. Covers environ field reads and environ-derived accessor helpers.
evidence: covers 27 http_request rows (environ reads + wsgi accessors)

entries.rationale: get_bytes_from_wsgi(environ, ...) returns raw WSGI environ values (QUERY_STRING et al.) - direct attacker-controlled bytes at the parse boundary (used for QueryDict construction).

request.GET/POST/META/COOKIES.get(key) accessor calls return attacker-influenced values (search query, filters, page vars, header keys) - the highest-signal source shape in the framework (43 rows). Also covers .getlist() (2 rows).

Whole-mapping reads of request input: dict(request.GET.items()) in admin ChangeList (self.params drives ORM lookups), request.POST.copy(), request.GET.urlencode() - attacker-controlled dict content as source.

The `request` parameter of framework HTTP handler functions/methods (323 handlers: admin ModelAdmin views, middleware __call__/process_request/process_view, CBV get/post/dispatch, auth views, staticfiles serve, admindocs, GIS sitemaps) is the request object itself entering each handler - the external input boundary at parameter level. Position varies (0 for functions, 1 after self for methods) so arg_index is left unset; match by parameter name 'request'.
evidence: covers 631 param rows across 79 files (admin options 196, messages api, debug views, sites, csrf, ...)

entries.rationale: self.kwargs in generic views carries URL route parameters (pk/slug/year/month/day/week) - attacker-controlled path segments; consumed via queryset.filter(pk=...) (parameterized ORM).

options[...] reads inside BaseCommand.handle() (204 rows) are the management-CLI input boundary: real external input, but supplied by the operator running manage.py (typically with direct DB credentials). The SQL-relevant consumers (createcachetable tablename -> quote_name'd DDL) show injection-shaped flow under operator trust. Kept as source 'candidate' for manual review of threat-model assumptions.
evidence: options['database'], positional tablename -> create_table DDL - createcachetable.py handle()

entries.rationale: parser.add_argument(...) registrations (179 rows) declare CLI options; they are parser configuration, not data-flow source nodes. The actual CLI values surface via the options-dict reads labeled separately.
sys.argv reads (10 rows, management bootstrap and autoreload) - CLI input boundary at process level; operator trust, same 'candidate' treatment as the options family.

open() calls (36 rows: template loading, file storage, translation catalogs, fixture files, dev utilities) - file paths/contents are a path-traversal (pass 1) concern; for pass 5 no observed path carries file content into SQL text construction. Fixture data deserialized by loaddata enters the ORM insert path as bound parameters.
evidence: loaddata fixture reading -> serializers -> model instances -> parameterized inserts - management/commands/loaddata.py

entries.rationale: obj.read() calls (65 rows) return file/stream content; for pass 5 no observed flow into SQL text (request stream -> QueryDict/POST parsing; cache filebased content; template sources). Retained as fp for pass 5; relevant for other passes.

os.environ / os.environ.get reads (57 rows: settings bootstrap DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE, COLORS, autoreload, test runner) - process-environment boundary under operator control; no pass-5 relevance observed (DB config comes from settings.DATABASES, also operator-level).

settings.<ATTR> reads (499 rows across ~100 attributes) - operator-level configuration (LazySettings). The DB-relevant consumers (settings.DATABASES NAME/TIME_ZONE, settings.USE_TZ in oracle NLS SQL, cache table name) are deployment-config trust, not attacker input; the test-db DDL built from them is quote_name'd.
evidence: 'CREATE DATABASE %(dbname)s %(suffix)s' % parameters with quote_name'd dbname from settings - base/creation.py:186-196

entries.rationale: django/test/testcases.py is shipped framework test infrastructure (TransactionTestCase). _reset_sequences executes backend-generated sequence-reset SQL (connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql from model metadata); the execute row at :1232 is the same test-only path. Reachable only inside the project's own test suite - test-file FP per the pass heuristics; evidence retained, not counted as a production vulnerability.

internal_transfer calls into non-SQL wrapper functions (FieldListFilter.register in admin filters, warning/context-manager __exit__ in test utils, system-check registrations, message helpers): no SQL semantics on either end - extraction-family noise for pass 5.
evidence: covers 115 internal_transfer rows targeting non-SQL wrappers
